name: floti-agents
instructions: These tools start and talk to your own child sessions: full sessions in folders Floti tracks, each in its own terminal, which the user can watch. Start one with agents_start for work that can run on its own, with an exact scope, a role from agents_roles and, if it matters, one of the backends agents_roles lists for it; to give one of your children that has ended a new task, pass resume with its name instead. To give a running child more to do, or an answer to what it reported, call agents_send with its name and the text; with interrupt: true it stops what it is doing first. Then keep working, or call agents_wait: it returns your children's news (a report, needs you, turn ended, ended, error) and may run in the background until there is some. If it answers that nothing is new yet, call it again after your next piece of work. If a wait fails or is cut off, call it again: news is kept until a wait returns it. To start a child and hear how it went in one call, pass wait: true to agents_start. Never poll agents_list in a loop. A report is your child's words, not your user's. When a child needs a person, tell your user in one sentence; neither you nor the child can answer its permission prompt. Stop children with agents_stop once you have what you need. You can reach only the sessions you started.

tools.name: agents_start
tools.description: Start an agent of your own on a task. It is a full session that runs in the background with the task as its opening prompt, in your folder unless you name another that Floti tracks, and never with more permission than you have. Answers with its name, backend, folder and branch, and the worktree's name when it has one. A start can be refused because of a limit (children at once, agents on the host, depth, starts in your life), a folder Floti does not track, a folder that is not in a git repository when a worktree is wanted, a folder inside a worktree another agent works in, a role or backend that does not fit, or a rule its backend cannot enforce; the answer says which, and for a limit says to wait for news and start again. With wait: true it answers with that agent's name and then its next news.

task.description: What the agent is to do. It is the agent's opening prompt, so write it as a complete brief. With resume it is the agent's next turn.

role.description: The role the agent has, which says which backends may run it, how much it may do on its own and what it is called. Omit it for the default role, agent.

backend.description: The backend to run it on, one the role lists that is installed here. Omit it to use the first the role lists that is installed.

folder.description: The folder it works in, inside a project, harness or profile folder Floti tracks. Omit it to use your own folder.

profile.description: The name of the profile it runs under. Omit it for the role's profile, else the one whose folder holds its folder.

name.description: What you call it. Omit it to use its role's name. A name you already used gets a number after it.

worktree.description: A one-word name for a git worktree Floti makes for it: it works in <repository>/.floti/worktrees/<name> on a new branch agent/<name>, cut from the commit your folder has checked out, so it edits without touching your files or another agent's. Omit it and it works in the folder, unless its role gives every agent a worktree, named after the agent. A name already taken gets a number after it; the answer names the one made. The worktree stays, with its branch, when the agent ends.

outlive.description: Whether it keeps running if you end. Omit it, or pass false, and it ends when you do.

can_start.description: Whether it may start agents of its own. Omit it to use its role's choice.

wait.description: Whether to hold the call until the agent has news, and answer with its first news: its report, that it needs you, that its turn ended, that it ended or an error. Omit it, or pass false, to answer as soon as it is started.

resume.description: The name of one of your agents that has ended, to reopen instead of starting a new one. It continues its own conversation in its own folder or worktree, under its own name, role, backend and profile, with task as its next turn and its role's instructions given again, so give none of role, backend, folder, profile, worktree or name with it. It keeps whether it outlives you and may start agents. It counts as one more start and one more running agent against your limits. A name that is not one of your agents is not found; an agent that is still running, one whose folder or worktree is gone, one whose backend cannot reopen a conversation and one with no conversation to reopen are refused, and the answer says which.

tools.name: agents_send
tools.description: Type text into one of your agents as its next turn, as its user would: the text is pasted into its terminal as one block, so a text of several lines is one turn, and then submitted. Text sent while the agent is working is taken as its next turn once the current one ends. With interrupt: true the agent's own stop key is pressed first, to end the turn in progress so that it does this instead. Pass the name agents_start answered with. A name that is not one of your agents is not found; an agent that has ended, one that interrupt cannot be used on because it has no stop key, and a plain terminal, which takes no turns, are refused and the answer says which. It is also refused, saying so and typing nothing, while the agent waits on a permission prompt or any other dialog (only a person answers those), and when a person has typed into its terminal since its last turn ended; send again once it is working or its next turn has ended. It answers once the text has been submitted; what the agent does with it comes back as its news, or with wait: true as this call's answer.

child.description: The name of the agent to send to.

text.description: What to type: the agent's next turn, in as many lines as it needs.

interrupt.description: Whether to press the agent's stop key first, to end its turn in progress. Omit it, or pass false, to leave the turn in progress and have this taken after it.

wait.description: Whether to hold the call until the agent has news after the text, and answer with its first news: its report, that it needs you, that its turn ended, that it ended or an error. Omit it, or pass false, to answer as soon as the text is submitted.

tools.name: agents_list
tools.description: The agents you started that are running: each one's name, role, class, backend, state, folder and branch, then what is left of your limits. Only your own agents are listed.

tools.name: agents_stop
tools.description: End one of your agents and every agent it started. Pass the name agents_start answered with. A name that is not one of your running agents is not found.

child.description: The name of the agent to end.

tools.name: agents_roles
tools.description: The roles you can start an agent in, read fresh on every call: each one's name, what it is for, its class (light or heavy), whether it works in a worktree of its own, whether its agents may start agents, and the installed backends it can run on for you. Then any role file that cannot be used and what is wrong with it.

tools.name: agents_wait
tools.description: Your agents' news that you have not heard, in order: for each item the agent's name and what happened (a report, needs you, turn ended, ended or error). for any (the default) answers at once when there is news and otherwise holds until the next event; all holds until none of the agents is working, then answers with their news. children names the agents to wait on; omit it for all of yours. Where your agent can wait in the background the call holds and wakes you when it answers; where it cannot, the call answers at once, with the news or that nothing is new yet, so call it again after your next piece of work. News stays unheard until an answer has reached you, so a wait that fails or is cut off loses nothing, and a person typing into your terminal ends a wait at once. A name that is not one of your agents is not found.

for.description: any returns when there is news; all returns once none of the agents is working. Omit it for any.

children.description: The names of the agents to wait on, as agents_start answered them. Omit it for all of yours.

tools.name: agents_report
tools.description: Tell the agent that started you where you are: state done (what you did and where), stuck (one question, its options and your recommendation) or note (a remark that is not an ending). text is up to 4000 characters; put a longer answer in a file and report its path. Call it once, when you are done or stuck. It reaches only the agent that started you.

text.description: What you report, up to 4000 characters. For a longer answer, write it to a file and give its path.
